description: Multiplayer Phase 1 prototype measurements (docs/multiplayer-research.plan.md §10–11), taken 15–16 October 2026 on the development M4 MacBook Air against a local `wrangler dev` room (server/), Chromium at 60 Hz vsync, High quality. Nothing here has crossed the internet yet: the deployed workers.dev run, cross-device test and Cloudflare free-plan message counting wait for the Cloudflare account. Load bots: server/tools/bots.mjs (walk a 6 m circle at 6 m/s, 10 poses/s).

r1RemoteSmoothness.description: Requirement R1 (smooth remote movement). One browser tab watches a second player walking a circle; each row is a 6 s sample of the remote avatar, measured per rendered frame. framesWithoutMovement counts frames where a walking avatar did not move (visible stutter). speedVariation is the coefficient of variation of displayed speed (0 = perfectly even).
r1RemoteSmoothness.targets: Plan §11: updated every frame, speed varies under 10% at a steady walk, no snaps over 10 cm except teleports. At 6 m/s and 60 fps an ordinary frame step is 10 cm, so maxStepCm 11.3–11.6 is normal walking plus the measured 5% speed variation, not a snap.

webkit.description: Playwright WebKit 26.5 (Safari's engine, headless, so ~48 fps) joined the same local room through the join dialog while one bot walked a circle. A sample of 6 s. Real Safari on the Mac and the iPad wait for the deployed server.
webkit.note: maxStepCm is one long headless frame (about 42 ms at 6 m/s), not a snap: speed per frame time varies by 6%.

r1RemoteSmoothness.unitSimulation: src/lib/game/net/__tests__/RemoteMotion.spec.ts runs the real PoseSender + RemoteMotion over simulated networks: delay stays ≤ 200 ms on a clean UK link and ≤ 300 ms with jitter, loss and bursts, with no frozen frames.

twentyPlayerSpike.description: The game tab in a world with 19 load bots (20 players, the per-world cap; a 21st connection is refused with 'This world is full'). Frames sampled over 6 s.

determinism.description: World generation fingerprints (src/lib/game/world/determinismReport.ts) in Node and in Playwright's Chromium, WebKit and Firefox, over the 3 pinned seeds plus 20 sweep seeds (/determinism/?dev&sweep=20). 'coarse' = what players see (heights to the mm, water type and level, lake and river counts, every tree's cell, species and variant); 'exact' = full float64 bit patterns.
determinism.exactMismatches: terrain and hydrology differ between engines on every seed (last-bit rounding of Math.tanh/pow and friends); trees match exactly
determinism.conclusion: No player-visible divergence, so the Q29-B maths fix isn't needed yet. tests/determinism.e2e.ts asserts the coarse hashes in all three engines.
